sections.html:
On the South Shore, Braintree had 39,143 residents in 2020 and covers about 14.6 square miles. Quincy lies to the north, Weymouth to the east, Holbrook to the south and Randolph to the west. South Shore Plaza is the best known retail destination, and Pond Meadow Park, Sunset Lake and part of the Blue Hills Reservation supply open space.

The town has two historic village centers, Braintree and South Braintree, and ZIP codes 02184 and 02185. The population grew from 10,580 in 1920 to 35,050 in 1970, so much of the housing was built in those decades, and when an older family home passes to heirs who live elsewhere, a quick sale can avoid showings and staging.

Officially it is the Town of Braintree, yet it has been a city under Massachusetts law since 2007, with a mayor and a town council. When you look for paperwork, note that the Assessors, the Collector and the Treasurer all sit under Municipal Finance on braintreema.gov.

sections.h2: Getting to Boston and the Cape
sections.html:
Braintree station is served by the MBTA Red Line, two commuter rail lines (the Fall River/New Bedford Line and the Kingston Line) and the seasonal CapeFLYER. The Weymouth Landing/East Braintree station on the Weymouth border is served by the Greenbush Line.

Interstate 93 and US 1 come in from Boston on the Southeast Expressway and head west toward Route 128. Route 3 splits south toward Cape Cod as the Pilgrims Highway, and Routes 37 and 53 are the other principal highways in town. A house close to the Red Line or an expressway ramp appeals to commuters, so say so when you talk to buyers. The same goes for a short walk to either village center, where shops and stations are close at hand.

Braintree averages about 48.6 inches of precipitation and about 61 inches of snow in a season, and totals swing widely. Nor'easters are the main storm threat, and thunderstorms from May to September can bring large hail and damaging winds. Roofs, gutters and basements draw the most questions from buyers' inspectors. If you have repair receipts or a recent roof date, keep them handy.

sections.h2: Tax rates and the Assessors' office
sections.html:
Fiscal 2026 rates from the Assessors, per $1,000 of assessed value:

Property classRate per $1,000
Residential$10.06
Commercial and industrial$21.39
Personal property$21.33

The Assessors' office is at 1 John F. Kennedy Memorial Drive, phone 781-794-8050. It helps owners with exemption forms, abatement forms and abutter lists, and it runs a property record website. Town Hall hours: Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesday to 7 p.m., Friday 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.

To contest your value, get an abatement application to the Assessors by the day the first actual bill is due. Where billing is quarterly that is generally February 1, and your own bill confirms the schedule.

An appeal starts with an abatement application to the Braintree Assessors, who get three months to act. If they say no, or say nothing, three more months are yours to appeal to the Appellate Tax Board.

  • Pay the bill on time, since the board may refuse a case otherwise, with limited exceptions.
  • Hearings take place at the board's Boston office or by video, usually lasting one to two hours for a single family case.
  • Waiting time for a hearing runs from four months to a year.
  • The burden is yours: show that fair cash value is under the assessed value. Comparable sales are the best proof.

A sale in the near future may close before the appeal ends, so ask your attorney who receives any refund.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Norfolk County
sections.html:
Norfolk County covers Braintree, and its Registry of Deeds takes $2.28 in excise tax per $500 of price or fraction of it at recording.

  • Recording a deed costs $156 in recorded land and $155 in registered land.
  • Pay the excise tax with its own attorney's check or bank check, apart from the recording fee.
  • Recording a municipal lien certificate adds an $81 fee.
  • Documents filed electronically avoid the $1 postage charge.

Your sale will need the Braintree fire department's certificate of compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Phone when a closing date exists, and plan for a fee. Alarms that are expired or undated get replaced.

Closings are attorney work in this state. Roughly 80 to 90 percent of properties are recorded land filed at the registry. A buyer's home inspection may be part of the deal, and for certain residential sales a seller cannot demand that the buyer waive it.

A septic system brings a Title 5 inspection, within two years before the sale. Find out whether your lot has one.

sections.h2: What to bring when you call
sections.html:
Calls go faster with a few items in front of you. Have your street address, the name on the tax bill, and the latest bill itself. Municipal Finance can tell you what is owed, and the Assessors can tell you what your property is valued at and whether an exemption applies. Write down names, dates and amounts as you go.

If the house came to you from a family member, have the paperwork that shows how it passed to you. Heirs who live out of town can handle most of the calls by phone and email.

Think about timing against the tax calendar too. Your bill lists its installment dates. If you sell between installments, the closing attorney works out how the year's tax is divided and what must be paid from your proceeds. Ask your attorney early so that figure is ready before you accept an offer, and so the net amount you compare is accurate. A municipal lien certificate gives the attorney the figure, and it carries a recording fee at the registry, so ask for it only when your attorney says it is needed.

Keep a list of any known problems with the house, such as a leaking roof, an old heating system or damp basement. A buyer who takes the house as it stands will still want to know, and being open about it speeds up an offer.

1. Phone the Assessors, 781-794-8050, to check your value and any exemption or open abatement.
  2. Ask Municipal Finance for your tax balance and request a municipal lien certificate if your attorney needs one.
  3. Check whether the house has septic.
  4. Book the fire department certificate once a date is set, and replace any expired alarms first.
  5. Have your attorney arrange two checks at the registry: one for the excise tax and one for the recording fee.

Cash Home Buyers buys Braintree houses as they are, so a direct sale cuts out showings, staging and repair negotiations. The tax payoff, the alarm certificate and the recording still happen at closing.

faqs.q: Is Braintree a city or town?
faqs.a: Legally a city since 2007, with a mayor and council, though the official name remains Town of Braintree.

faqs.q: What is the residential tax rate in Braintree?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2026 the Braintree Assessors list $10.06 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Norfolk County?
faqs.a: $2.28 per $500 of the price or fraction of it, collected by the Norfolk County Registry of Deeds at recording.
Braintree station has the Red Line, the Fall River/New Bedford and Kingston commuter rail lines, and seasonal CapeFLYER service. The Greenbush Line stops at Weymouth Landing/East Braintree.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell a house in Braintree?
faqs.a: Yes, the town fire department has to certify your alarms before a sale.
